skill.displayName: 收入与成本截止性核对（免费版）

llm.summary: The checker itself is local, but the skill also pushes users into a paid upgrade flow and writes a temporary upsell marker despite presenting itself as no-payment and no-network.

dimensions.detail: Read and Bash are proportionate for running the local Node checker, but the runtime reads session-related environment variables for upsell suppression rather than for cutoff analysis.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer, package dependency, remote payload retrieval, or post-install hook was found in the artifact files.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill claims no payment and no network in its metadata and overview, yet later requires agents to present an upsell and, if the user selects paid, complete a purchase flow and return checkout material.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The script writes a marker file under the OS temp directory to track whether the upsell has been shown, which is disclosed only indirectly and is unrelated to the checking function.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The implemented cutoff checks are purpose-aligned, but the instructions and runtime output add a commercial purchase flow for a paid version, including payment-link/QR-code handling, which is outside the core document-checking purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. The local cutoff checker does not appear to exfiltrate data or execute remote code, but users should know it includes mandatory paid-upgrade messaging, may direct an agent into a payment flow, and writes a temporary marker to track whether that prompt has been shown. Use SKILL_NO_UPSELL=1 if installed and you do not want the commercial prompt.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Partly supported: the actual engine performs cutoff checks, but artifact comments and one insufficient-input message refer to share-based-payment material, creating business-purpose confusion.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Supported in part: no network code was found, but the skill text and runtime output instruct agents toward an external purchase/payment flow despite no-network/no-payment framing.
[AE1] expected: Downgraded: scripts/run.mjs is present in this workspace and was fully inspected.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Supported: the paid-upgrade instructions and runtime upsell are material behavior beyond a local cutoff-checking skill, and the engine header also contains mismatched share-based-payment wording.
[LP1] expected: Partly supported but limited: the script reads environment variables, but only to control or suppress upsell prompts; this is not needed for analysis and should be disclosed more clearly.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Supported as a review concern: the trigger language is broad for a skill that always includes commercial messaging after normal output.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded for security adjudication: the skill is primarily Chinese-language accounting workflow content, which may affect usability but does not by itself show malicious behavior.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Supported: payment orchestration, session-env use, and temp-marker persistence are not necessary for the stated local checker.
[A.I.G SARIF] expected: The static scan reported no T01-T09 results; artifact review still found non-malicious review concerns from the skill's own text and runtime behavior.
